Honestly it would be better if they stopped the sugar subsidy and placed a higher tax on sugary food and beverages. Refined sugar is almost poison. The reason we have so much obesity and diabetes isn't trans fat, it's sugar and carbs.

The subsidy is on corn, not sugar. Everything in the US is loaded with corn syrup (which is much worse for you than normal sugar). Real sugar has import tariffs to protect the Domino monopoly and actually costs more in the US than overseas.

Trans fats have already been replaced in a large portion of prepared food. This really just shows how useless the FDA is. Public opinion has pushed states to ban trans fats and restaurants that operate across the nation changed years ago to appease those states. This seems more like a move to force those who still want/need hydrogenated oils in their products to file for permission, bringing money in to the FDA than it is to protect consumers.

From the article:

The FDA estimates trans fat consumption declined about 78% between 2003 and 2012 after the labeling went into effect.

  1. The FDA is taking credit for a decline that is most likely a result of other actions (such as fast food places eliminating trans fats, public opinion shifting in that time frame, etc)
  2. A 78% decrease in trans fats and Americans are still unhealthy. So banning (or allowing with permission) the remaining 22% is going to make a difference? Did we all shift to other foods when McDonalds stopped frying with oils that had trans fats?

TLDR; Seems more like a move to generate income and get some good press while really doing nothing.

I've noticed trans fats recently getting replaced with coconut and palm oils (which are some of the very rare natural fats that similar to trans fat). Betting this is prompted by coconut and/or palm lobbies.

The other possible motive for an FDA ban is that they discovered some health benefit of trans fat. No way in hell would they ever act in our best interest. Yes, I'm completely serious.
